![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14227574/assets/1d4df2d201ccbaf2305534d61c8a0ed5f7957b1629d8cd2fbd5fff933283c0dc.png)

The scatter plot above shows the number of matches won by some chess players in a championship and the hours they spend training per day.
Use the trend line to estimate how much time players need to train each day to win $30$ championship games.
question.worked_solution:
To make our estimation, we proceed as follows:

- We start at $y=30$ on the vertical axis.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14227574/assets/26ba10258a8794a97dfc5e61c8160b342ed6890f7a9af40c1e21ac814c779188.png)

- Then, we move right until we intersect the trend line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14227574/assets/e50d79adb9803f6509314cf3512fcd388ccc78b287d6653b9e318ce54ce45022.png)

- Finally, we move down until we intersect the horizontal axis.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14227574/assets/a9bd5a7973ecb2e88c328d0943d4bfebe9862b2cea1abbd0b3fa3665fa177167.png)

Therefore, a chess player that wins $30$ games spends around $5$ hours training per day.
